## Feasibility result

No device can satisfy all stated requirements simultaneously.

A rack consuming 10 kW continuously produces 10 kW of heat. A sealed, water-free, non-refrigerated device with no ventilation, moving parts, external heat sink, or below-ambient contact has no permitted continuous path for that heat to leave.

It can only:

- store heat temporarily, causing the rack to warm;
- transfer heat to its enclosure or surroundings, requiring a temperature rise;
- radiate heat outward, which also requires the emitting surface to be warmer than its surroundings.

Therefore, keeping the rack exactly at ambient temperature indefinitely while continuously rejecting 10 kW is incompatible with the constraints.

## Closest possible portfolios

| Option | Constraint relaxed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Passive enclosure conduction | Permit heat flow into an external thermal mass or structure | Silent and sealed, but requires temperature rise and an external heat sink |
| Passive radiation | Permit a large external radiating surface | No moving parts or electricity, but the radiator must run above ambient |
| Thermal storage | Permit finite temperature rise | Works only for a limited duration |
| Heat pipe or thermosyphon | Permit internal fluid motion and heat transfer to an external sink | Silent, but still needs a heat-rejection surface |
| Refrigeration | Permit electricity and refrigerant | Can maintain near-ambient temperature, but violates multiple constraints |
| Ventilated air cooling | Permit ventilation and fans or natural airflow | Can reject 10 kW, but violates sealing and ventilation requirements |
| Water cooling | Permit water, pumps, and an external radiator | Practical, but violates water-free and moving-part requirements |

The minimum necessary change is to allow at least one continuous heat-rejection mechanism and accept either an external sink or a temperature above ambient. Without that, the requested design space is empty.
